newsitem.title: UK: Coopers&Lybrand sets writs on 9 Barings employees.
newsitem.headline: Coopers&Lybrand sets writs on 9 Barings employees.

text.p: British-based accountancy firm Coopers & Lybrand on Friday issued writs against nine former directors and employees of collapsed investment bank Barings.

The firm told Britain's PA news agency the purpose of the move was to join the former employees in a legal action already being taken against Coopers and other parties by the administrators of Barings.
The bank collapsed in early 1995 after rogue trader Nick Leeson racked up losses of $1.4 billion. It is now part of Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV.

"Despite the fact that we are not responsible for the collapse of Barings, we face a substantial claim. We are perceived to have deep pockets which are available to those who have lost money," Coopers & Lybrand said in a statement.
"We are confident our work was properly carried out," the accounting firm added.
